trust_decision.summary: Decided per MCP tool call: whether a caller may receive the Pipeline replay script (mainScript plus loadedScripts), which the fix treats as the job's pipeline source equivalent to config.xml, by a single Item.EXTENDED_READ check on run.getParent() inside DefaultMcpServer.getReplayScripts; at the pinned commit that method reads ReplayAction.getOriginalScript() with no permission check of any kind (only the dispatcher-wide Jenkins.READ), and the fix returns an empty script instead of throwing when the check fails.

landing_point.why: The advisory says a Pipeline's script can be read without the config.xml permission; an engineer looks first at the tool that reads the script out of ReplayAction and returns it in GetReplayScriptsResult.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool getReplayScripts (tool call over /mcp-server/mcp, /mcp-server/sse or /mcp-server/stateless, invoked through McpToolWrapper)
fix_sites.module_kind: McpServerExtension tool handler in the default extension class

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getBuildScm reports the SCM a build actually checked out (the git BuildData recorded on the build, i.e. build output shown on the build page), not the job configuration, so a solver can argue it sits outside the config.xml/ExtendedRead rule the fix cites.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A caller that does hold Item.EXTENDED_READ must still receive the full mainScript and loadedScripts, and a non-replayable build must still fail with 'Not a replayable Pipeline build'; the plugin's established convention next to the sink is to answer with an empty value (getJobScm returns List.of()) rather than throw, so the guard must not be added as a blanket AccessDeniedException or moved into the shared build lookup where it would also block build-level data that Item.READ holders legitimately read.

O6_input_shapes: jobFullName only, resolving to the last build
denied result keeps the structured-output shape: mainScript empty string and loadedScripts an empty map, not null and not an error

O8_uncovered_routes.route: getBuildScm returns the build's SCM configuration (same GitScmConfig record, same GitScmUtil helper) with no permission check at all, while its job-level sibling getJobScm gates the identical payload on Item.EXTENDED_READ
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: BuildData-based SCM info is build output, not the job's config.xml, so the advisory's pipeline-source rule does not reach it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one file over from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: findJobsWithScmUrl enumerates every job via Jenkins.getAllItems and returns matching Job beans to any caller holding Overall/Read, with no Item.READ or Item.EXTENDED_READ filtering
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a search helper keyed on an SCM URL; it returns which jobs match, no script or configuration body, so it can be called a discovery tool rather than a disclosure path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the previous route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a getJobConfig-style tool, or a workflow-cps @Exported job property, disclosing the job's CpsFlowDefinition through the existing getJob/serialize path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This repository has now made the same mistake twice (getJobScm fixed under SECURITY-3622, getReplayScripts fixed here), and the README tells third-party plugins to add @Tool methods, so a job-level script/config reader without the EXTENDED_READ gate is exactly what a maintainer would write next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a tool returning a Run or Job whose stapler export starts including an action or property that carries the script (ReplayAction or the flow definition)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Serialization is generic here: any action/property that gains @ExportedBean starts being emitted with no per-value permission logic, so the leak would appear without anyone touching the tool that reads it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a build-scoped script reader ('what did this build run') built like getBuildScm, on the same Run lookup and with the same missing gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adjacent build-scoped tool already omits every Item permission check, so copying its shape for a script getter reproduces the flaw.

O9_family: Missing authorization / improper access control (CWE-862): a read tool discloses job configuration-equivalent data without the Item permission Jenkins core requires

O10_build.toolchain: Maven with org.jenkins-ci.plugins:plugin parent 6.2138.v03274d462c13, hpi packaging, spotless check enabled
services: local git binary for GitSampleRepoRule-based tests
O10_build.project_tests: ReplayRebuildTest (src/test/java/io/jenkins/plugins/mcp/server/extensions/ReplayRebuildTest.java) covers rebuildBuild, getReplayScripts happy path and non-Pipeline failure, and replayBuild, but has no permission test at the pinned commit; JobScmExtensionTest covers getJobScm/getBuildScm/getBuildChangeSets/findJobsWithScmUrl with no authorization test either.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard the tool with job.hasPermission(Item.READ) (the intuitive 'can read the job' permission) or lean on the dispatcher's existing Jenkins.READ check, instead of matching the Item.EXTENDED_READ boundary used for config.xml and getJobScm.

out_of_scope_notes: The dispatcher requires only Jenkins.READ for every tool (McpToolWrapper.java:321), so other tools (getBuild, getBuildLog, searchBuildLog, getTestResults, getBuildChangeSets, updateBuild) never check Item.READ on the target job; that is a broader authorization gap than this advisory's script disclosure, noted once and not pursued.
